title: The new zone source text keeps the City map's answer and the word 'today' in the .3dm, so both go stale and the store: none licence is broken
detail: lookup_choices now writes saved_ui['zone_source'] = 'suggested by Gordium · City zoning map says R-1b (checked today)'. The key has no '_' prefix, so storable_ui keeps it and _save_ui_state writes it into the .3dm at Draw. _drawn also copies it into fact_sources (the panel and report lines). Three results: (1) The City zoning map (endpoints.yaml city_zoning: 'store: none', 'May not be reproduced or redistributed') now has its answer ('says R-1b') stored with the project. The code's own comment says this may never happen. (2) Open the file a week later and use Edit site…: _box_state.source('zone') reads saved_ui['zone_source'] before anything else, so the box still says '(checked today)'. On a later Draw, fact_sources stores that same text with the new date, so the report reads 'City zoning map says R-1b (checked today) · confirmed by you, <a later date>'. That claims the map was checked on a day it was not. (3) Say the architect looks up R-1b, switches the dropdown to R-1a and presses Draw. keep() sets state['zone_source'] to ENTERED, but nothing ever replaces saved_ui['zone_source']; only lookup_choices touches it. When the box reopens, R-1a is shown as 'suggested by Gordium · City zoning map says R-1b (checked today)'. A re-Draw then stores that text as R-1a's source, confirmed by you.
evidence: rhino_logic.py:872 `saved_ui["zone_source"] = SUGGESTED + " · City zoning map" + (" says " + known[0] if len(known) == 1 else "") + " (checked today)"`; rhino_logic.py:791-794 `storable_ui` keeps every key not starting with '_'; gordium_rhino.py:858 `doc.Strings.SetString(SECTION, UI_ENTRY, json.dumps(logic.storable_ui(state)))`; gordium_rhino.py:1234 `return saved_ui.get(key + "_source") or (sources.get(key) or {}).get("source") ...`; gordium_rhino.py:1668 `sources.update(logic.fact_sources(state, time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"), confirmed=True))`; endpoints.yaml city_zoning `store: none`. Checked by running it: `storable_ui(lookup_choices({'status':'found','facts':{'zone':{'value':'R-1b'}}},{},{},zones=['R-1a','R-1b'])[1])` returns `{'zone_source': 'suggested by Gordium · City zoning map says R-1b (checked today)', ...}`.
pin: test_lookup_box.py: after lookup_choices for R-1b, assert that storable_ui(saved) has no key whose value contains 'R-1b' or 'today' (the live wording is a session '_' key only). Also assert that fact_sources(state with that source, a later date) does not say 'today' and does not name the map's district.
suggested_fix: Keep the live wording ('City zoning map says R-1b, checked <the lookup's date>') in a session key (e.g. saved_ui['_zone_source']) that _box_state reads first, and store only a plain non-dated source (e.g. 'suggested by Gordium · City zoning map, used live') under the storable 'zone_source', or put the lookup's actual YYYY-MM-DD in the session wording. Also, when the box's district differs from the looked-up one at Draw, write state['zone_source'] back into saved_ui (or drop saved_ui['zone_source']), so a stale 'suggested' never outranks the architect's own pick on reopen.
skeptics:
I could not refute the main claim. The finding holds, but parts of it are less serious than stated or were already there before this PR.

What I read:
- rhino_logic.py:871-873 (new) writes saved_ui["zone_source"] = SUGGESTED + " · City zoning map" + " says <zone>" + " (checked today)". On 7944f83 (line 820) the same key was written as SUGGESTED + " · " + label("zone","zone"), which falls back to "City zoning map, used live". That text had no district name and no date.
- rhino_logic.py:791-794: storable_ui drops only keys that start with "_". So zone_source survives, and gordium_rhino.py:858 (_save_ui_state, called from _drawn at 1666) writes it into the .3dm.
- gordium_rhino.py:1233-1238: when the box reopens, _box_state.source("zone") reads saved_ui["zone_source"] first, before fact_sources.

(2) Stale "(checked today)": confirmed, and new in this PR. The phrase is saved into the .3dm. When the file is reopened on a later day, Edit site… shows it again. Note that _apply_box (gordium_rhino.py:1265-1287) never rewrites zone_source. After that, the next Draw saves the stale text into fact_sources with the new day's date (gordium_rhino.py:1668 and rhino_logic.py:1133). The result is a record saying the map was checked on a day it was not. That breaks the "everything is traceable" principle.

(3) Switching the dropdown after a lookup: real, but only partly new. keep() and zone_picked (gordium_ui.py:673, rhino_logic.py:769) set state["zone_source"] = ENTERED, and the fact_sources written at that Draw are correct. But saved_ui["zone_source"] keeps the lookup text, and it is preferred when the box reopens. That stale-source path already existed on 7944f83, with the vaguer wording. What this PR adds is the clear contradiction: the box shows "R-1a · … City zoning map says R-1b".

(1) The store: none point: weaker. facts["zone"] = R-1b was already stored at Draw before this PR, with a "City zoning map" source. Still, the new text does store the map's answer word for word, which the comment on line 871 says must not happen.

Point (2) on its own is a real defect that this PR introduces, so the finding stands.

I could not refute this one. I ran the cited call: storable_ui keeps the new zone_source text 'suggested by Gordium · City zoning map says R-1b (checked today)', and gordium_rhino.py:858 (_save_ui_state at Draw, via _drawn at 1662-1670) writes it into the .3dm. Nothing ever overwrites saved_ui['zone_source'] apart from lookup_choices (rhino_logic.py:857 and 872). _apply_box (gordium_rhino.py:1265-1287) copies ground, buffer and checked from the state into saved_ui, but not zone_source. zone_picked (rhino_logic.py:769) only sets state['zone_source']=ENTERED, and the 'ticked' carry-over (gordium_rhino.py:1554) lasts only for that box session. When the box reopens, _box_state's source() (gordium_rhino.py:1233-1238) reads saved_ui['zone_source'] before anything else. So: (2) a later session still shows '(checked today)', and the next Draw saves it again through fact_sources (rhino_logic.py:1133) with that day's date. (3) After the architect switches the dropdown to R-1a and draws, the reopened box shows R-1a with the text 'City zoning map says R-1b (checked today)', and a re-Draw stores that as R-1a's confirmed source. Part of this is older than the diff: zone_source was already stored without a '_' prefix and already went stale on 7944f83, as the generic 'City zoning map, used live'. What this diff adds is the persisted 'says <zone>' and '(checked today)', which turn the stale text into a wrong date and a wrong district. Point (1), the store: none breach, is weaker. facts['zone'] already holds the suggested district on purpose, and the comment at 871 treats the district as fine to keep. Points (2) and (3), though, are clearly real and come from this diff.

title: Picking a district updates Draw and its reason but not the source label beside the dropdown, which can still say 'not set' or name another district
detail: The zone row's source label is built once from box_rows when the box opens. For the new no-district case that text is '— · not set', so the label reads 'not set'. The new zone_changed handler calls zone_picked and refreshes draw.Enabled and reason.Text, but never this label. After the R-2a lookup, the architect picks R-1b and ticks I confirm: Draw turns on, yet the row still reads 'R-1b  not set  [I confirm]'. Likewise, after an R-1b lookup and a switch to R-1a, the label beside R-1a still reads 'suggested by Gordium · City zoning map says R-1b (checked today)', although zone_picked has already set zone_source to ENTERED. The box contradicts itself on the exact path round 1 fixed.
evidence: gordium_ui.py:734 `layout.AddRow(title, row(zone, label(r["text"].split(" · ", 1)[-1], size=11), confirm))` (an inline label, never kept or updated); gordium_ui.py:709-712 `def zone_changed(s, e): logic.zone_picked(...); draw.Enabled = ...; reason.Text = logic.draw_reason(state)`; rhino_logic.py:714-716 `... if state.get("zone") else "— · not set"`.
pin: A logic-level test: after zone_picked(state, 'R-1b', None), the zone row from box_rows(state) reads 'R-1b · entered by you'. A wiring check in test_lookup_box.py asserts that zone_changed sets the zone source label's Text from box_rows (e.g. `zone_note.Text =` inside zone_changed). Both must fail if the label refresh is removed.
suggested_fix: Keep the zone source label in a variable (zone_note). In zone_changed, after zone_picked, set zone_note.Text from the zone row's text in logic.box_rows(state), using the same split(' · ', 1)[-1], so the label always matches state['zone'] and state['zone_source'].
skeptics: The finding holds. I read apps/rhino_plugin/gordium_ui.py on 5937781. Line 733 builds the zone row's source text once, as an inline `label(r["text"].split(" · ", 1)[-1], size=11)`. No variable keeps that label, and nothing updates it later. The new `zone_changed` handler at lines 709-714 calls logic.zone_picked, then refreshes draw.Enabled and reason.Text, but it never touches that label and never calls done(), so the box is not rebuilt. In packages/design_checker/design_checker/rhino_logic.py, lines 713-715 (new in this PR) make the text "— · not set" when no zone is set, so the label reads "not set". zone_picked at lines 764-770 sets state["zone"] and switches zone_source to ENTERED whenever the pick differs from the opening district. So in the no-district case: the architect picks R-1b and ticks I confirm, Draw turns on, and the label beside the dropdown still says "not set". That contradiction is new to this PR, because the base preselected index 0, its text was always "<zone> · <source>", and it had no live handler that turned Draw on. The second scenario (R-1b looked up, then R-1a picked, label still says "suggested by Gordium…") is partly older: on 7944f83 the label at line 733 was just as static. Even so, this PR now sets zone_source to ENTERED straight away while the label still names the old source, so the box contradicts its own state. It is a real display inconsistency on the exact path this PR changed.

I could not refute it. The source label never updates, so the finding stands.

- **The label is fixed when the box opens.** At apps/rhino_plugin/gordium_ui.py:734 the zone row is drawn with `row(zone, label(r["text"].split(" · ", 1)[-1], size=11), confirm)`. That label is a throwaway inline object. No variable keeps it, so nothing can change it later.
- **Its text comes from the state at opening time.** box_rows (packages/design_checker/design_checker/rhino_logic.py:713-715) builds it as `zone · zone_source`, or `— · not set` when no district is set.
- **The new handler updates two things, not three.** zone_changed (gordium_ui.py:709-714, added in this diff) calls logic.zone_picked, which sets zone and sets zone_source to ENTERED when the pick differs from first_zone (rhino_logic.py:764-770). It then refreshes draw.Enabled and reason.Text, and never touches the source label.
- **Nothing rebuilds the box after a pick.** Choosing from the dropdown does not go through pick() and does not close the dialog, so the stale label stays on screen.
- **The 'not set' case is new and reachable.** This diff removed the auto-select of index 0 (gordium_ui.py:645). With no district set, the dropdown opens with nothing picked and the label reads 'not set'. Picking R-1b and ticking 'I confirm' turns Draw on, while the label beside R-1b still says 'not set'.

Part of this is older than the PR. The second scenario (switching from a looked-up R-1b to R-1a while the label still says 'suggested by Gordium · City zoning map...') existed on 7944f83, because the label was already static there. That base also had no zone_changed handler. This PR raises its priority, since the in-box state (zone_source=ENTERED, Draw on) now moves on a pick while the label beside it does not. Neither case leads to a false pass: Draw still depends on can_draw and the confirm tick. This is a UI contradiction, not a wrong verdict.
